changes.old: “‘One does not conclude the paschal offering with an afikoman’—
changes.new: “‘One does not eat dessert after the paschal offering’—
changes.reason: Use the same accurate rendering of the repeated Mishnah quotation.

changes.old: to this they answer: you do not interrogate or conclude after the Paschal mystery;
changes.new: to this they answer: one does not eat dessert after the paschal offering;
changes.reason: Preserve the actual repeated Mishnah quotation. The inherited phrase about interrogating a Paschal mystery is explanatory material that replaced the quotation.

changes.old: “that he questioned whether it means together, or like it diminished of its pit”—
changes.new: “That which the Mishnah teaches, ‘and like its pit,’ is what he asks about: What does it mean—like it and its pit together, or perhaps it means like it without its pit?”—
changes.reason: Restore the omitted wording of the Rashi quotation, which the inherited English reduced to a short summary.

changes.old: For the purification of water operates through hashakah (confluent contact with the living spring);
changes.new: For the purification of water operates through hashakah (contact between waters);
changes.reason: The Hebrew says hashakah. The added requirement of a living spring is unsupported and misleading, since the passage itself discusses a mikveh.

changes.old: “Whoever is greater than his fellow, his evil inclination is greater than he.”
changes.new: “Whoever is greater than his fellow has a greater evil inclination than his fellow’s.”
changes.reason: גדול הימנו compares the person’s inclination with his fellow’s; it does not say that the inclination is greater than the person himself.

changes.old: “Our father Jacob did not die, etc. He said to him: I derive this from an explicit scriptural verse.”
changes.new: “Our father Jacob did not die, etc. He said to him: I am expounding a scriptural verse.”
changes.reason: מקרא אני דורש describes interpretation of a verse. Calling it an explicit verse obscures the author’s immediate contrast between the plain sense and derash.

changes.old: that had he known with absolute certainty that he was physically from the lineage of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob,
changes.new: that had he known with certainty that he was descended from Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob,
changes.reason: Remove the unsupported restriction physically; the following phrase explains this in terms of holiness at the root of one’s birth.

changes.old: meaning that in the very biological root of his birth he was bound up in sacred lineage,
changes.new: meaning that at the very root of his birth he was bound up in holiness,
changes.reason: Restore בקדושה as holiness; biological and sacred lineage were unsupported additions.

changes.old: For curses and reprimands exist so that through them Israel constrict themselves in sacred discipline;
changes.new: For curses and punishments exist so that through them Israel constrict themselves in sacred discipline;
changes.reason: עונשין means punishments, not reprimands.

changes.old: that through warnings and admonitions awe is deepened all the more;
changes.new: that through warnings and punishments awe is deepened all the more;
changes.reason: Preserve both distinct terms: אזהרות warnings and עונשין punishments.

changes.old: “Yea also, because he transgresses by wine, he is a proud man, neither keeps at home.”
changes.new: “Indeed, wine betrays the proud man, and he does not remain at ease.”
changes.reason: Render the verse as the author reads it in the next phrases: the wine betrays the proud man and becomes sadness. The inherited English changes the agency to a man transgressing by wine.

changes.old: saying to them: Behold your precious love before the Omnipresent; its removal is fresh like its initial setting-out.”
changes.new: saying to them: See how beloved you are before the Omnipresent; the bread is the same when removed as when first set out.”
changes.reason: חבתכם לפני המקום means how beloved you are to God; the inherited English ambiguously makes it the pilgrims’ own love.

changes.old: that in Shabbat there are 39 forbidden categories of creative labor, and corresponding to them in tzitzit are 39 coilings (chulyot);
changes.new: that in Shabbat there are 39 forbidden categories of creative labor, and corresponding to them in tzitzit are 39 windings;
changes.reason: כריכות are windings, not chulyot, which are groups of windings.

changes.old: and there remain 8 additional labors (building, demolishing, igniting, extinguishing, striking the final blow, and carrying).
changes.new: and there remain 8 additional labors.
changes.reason: Remove the incomplete explanatory list, which names six despite announcing eight and is absent from the canonical Hebrew. The source simply says eight remain.

changes.old: And since Scripture was required to explicitly admonish against this, it implies that it is a statement containing factual reality that wounds through verbal oppression;
changes.new: And since it was necessary to warn against this, it implies that it is something that could be said and would constitute verbal oppression;
changes.reason: Restore the phrasing of the inference without the unsupported attribution of this exact warning to Scripture.

changes.old: And they stated there (59b): Why did the Torah issue warnings regarding converts in thirty-six places? Because their natural leaning is fraught;
changes.new: And they stated there (59b): Why did the Torah issue warnings concerning converts? Because their inclination is bad;
changes.reason: Translate סורן רע directly and remove the added thirty-six places, which is absent from the quoted source excerpt.

changes.old: meaning their biological ancestral foundation is rooted in paganism,
changes.new: meaning that their root and foundation are indeed bad,
changes.reason: The inherited biological ancestry and paganism gloss replaces the Hebrew שרשן ויסודן באמת רע with an unsupported interpretation. Preserve the author’s words without adding a biological claim.

changes.old: And as I likewise heard, that usually that which is coveted by physical eyes—
changes.new: And as I likewise heard, that generally what is desirable to the eyes—
changes.reason: Remove physical, which conflicts with the next phrase specifying the eyes as a symbol of wisdom.

changes.old: when viewed from the perspective of inner wisdom attributed to spiritual vision—is not at all pleasing to the eyes of mortals;
changes.new: from the perspective of wisdom, which is associated with the eye—is not pleasing to human eyes;
changes.reason: Preserve the distinction between symbolic vision associated with wisdom and outward human appearance.

changes.old: which constitutes the oral sanctification of the Oral Torah,
changes.new: which is the holiness of the Oral Torah,
changes.reason: קדושת תורה שבעל פה is the holiness of the Oral Torah, not oral sanctification.

changes.old: since the Blessed Name boasts, as it were, counter to all creation: “For that he also is flesh”—retaining divine transcendence even in bodily form.
changes.new: since the Blessed Name asserts His greatness in comparison with him: “For he, too, is flesh.”
changes.reason: לנגדו refers to Moses. The inherited translation changes this to all creation and adds an unsupported statement about retaining divine transcendence in bodily form.

changes.old: The inner reason is because those earliest generations stood aligned facing the royalty of the Davidic dynasty,
changes.new: The point is that the earliest generations corresponded to the kingship of the house of David,
changes.reason: נגד here expresses correspondence, not opposition or merely standing facing a dynasty.

changes.old: and the month of Menachem Av is the ninth month in the cycle of months (counting from Nisan),
changes.new: and the month of Av is associated with the ninth letter of the alphabet,
changes.reason: אות תשיעית means ninth letter, Tet. Av is not the ninth month from Nisan; the inherited calendar explanation is erroneous.

changes.old: and in Av, which is the ninth month embodying life, the Temple was destroyed,
changes.new: and in Av, which corresponds to the ninth letter, signifying life, the Temple was destroyed,
changes.reason: Correct the repeated mistranslation of ninth letter as ninth month.

changes.reason: בכח גדול qualifies how the scholars draw down the light. Fierce and unyielding were unsupported attributes attached to the divine light.
